data.cultural_impact: The Roman name Silvanus is rooted in the ancient pagan belief of a deity in charge of forest protection and agriculture. This might have influenced the Christian naming of someone as Silvanus, suggesting a connection to the natural world, as well as an affinity towards farming, gardening, or nature.
data.spiritual_significance: For early Christians, adopting a pagan name like Silvanus signified their belief in the power of Christ transforming even the old gods into something new and holy. Silvanus, as a Christian name, could have symbolized believing in the ultimate sovereignty of Christianity over pagan beliefs, while embracing the protective and nurturing aspects of nature.

historical_references.reference: Silvanus was an early Christian bishop and martyr, venerated as a saint. He was a disciple of St. Paul and is mentioned in several of his letters. According to tradition, Silvanus was the bishop of Calabria in southern Italy, and he was martyred during the persecutions of Emperor Decius in the mid-third century.

Silvanus is also the name of a Roman god of the woodlands and forests. The name is derived from the Latin word 'silva', meaning 'forest'. Silvanus was sometimes identified with Dionysus, the Greek god of the wild, and was believed to protect crops and animals. The name may have been adopted by early Christians as a way to disguise their faith during periods of religious persecution.
historical_references.time_period: Roman Republic to Roman Empire (circa 500 BC to 5th century AD)

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Silvanus, derived from the Roman god of forests and fertility, has seen a modern revival in various contexts. In religious spaces, it is often used as a given name for study groups focused on the Bible, reflecting the spiritual connection to nature. In the realm of ecology, environmental organizations and individuals may adopt the name as a nod to ancient deities who presided over forests. In the tech sector, Silvanus is a popular name for startups that emphasize sustainability, growth, and innovation.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Ruth Silvanus in Athens, Greece credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Silvanus, which means "Forester, Protector". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Silvanus is a Roman name derived from the god Silvanus, the protector of forests, fields, and shepherds. In Christian tradition, Silvanus is venerated as a patron saint of forests and forests dwellers, and is believed to protect travelers and those who live in the woods. His name symbolizes the connection between nature and spirituality, and the idea that even in the wilderness, one can find God's presence.
